newsitem.title: UK: Babcock to buy Rosyth Dockyard in Scotland.
newsitem.headline: Babcock to buy Rosyth Dockyard in Scotland.

text.p: British engineering firm Babcock International Group Plc said on Monday the British Ministry of Defence agreed to sell it the Rosyth Royal Dockyard in Scotland after more than two years of negotiations.
Babcock has commercially managed the dockyard, which has annual sales of over 200 million pounds ($336.6 million), since 1987.

As part of the deal, the Ministry of Defence allocated a programme of work stretching over the next 10 years to refit nuclear submarines, aircraft carriers, destroyers, frigates and smaller war vessels, Babcock said in a statement.
In addition, the yard will be able to compete for a substantial programme of unallocated workload.

"The acquisition of Rosyth will not only enable Babcock International to enhance further the yard's competitiveness but also provide the group with an opportunity to develop and diversify the Rosyth facility," the company said.
Earlier this year, the British government agreed to sell Rosyth's rival dockyard, Devonport in Plymouth, to DML, the U.S.-led consortium that manages that yard.
